task: Validate BASIQ CDR consent flow against production API surface; flag rate limits, sandbox vs prod contradictions, and ADR sponsor SLA obligations

findings.summary: BASIQ sandbox does not mirror production CDR consent scopes — sandbox exposes all scopes unconditionally; production requires live ADR accreditation and consumer consent per holder.
BASIQ rate limits differ per plan tier — sandbox is effectively uncapped; production Starter caps at 300 req/min per connection. MAAT batch reconciliation could hit this.
ADR sponsor obligations require MAAT to have a registered software product under an accredited ADR before calling live data holders. Sponsor SLA includes incident reporting within 30 mins.
CDR Phase 3 payment initiation not yet live for BASIQ — watch trigger for MAAT v2 payment flows. Estimated 2026 Q3 rollout.

contradictions.summary: Sandbox test results cannot be used as proof of production CDR compliance — the two environments are architecturally different. Any REAL status on MAAT BASIQ integration requires a production test run.

opportunities.summary: MAAT can use BASIQ pre-built consent UI to reduce ADR build cost and time-to-accreditation. This path is faster than building consent flows from scratch.

risks.summary: Proceeding to production without ADR accreditation confirmation exposes MAAT to CDR enforcement action from ACCC. Block go-live gate on this.

notes: F01 and CONTRADICTION-01 are hard blockers for REAL status on MAAT BASIQ integration. COAX-G must not mark closed until production test run exists.
